question.problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola 

$$
x-4=3{t}^{2},\,y+2=6t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(y\,+$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x-4}{3},\,t=\frac{y+2}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{y+2}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{x-4}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{36} & =\frac{x-4}{3} \\ (y+2)^{2} & =36\cdot (\frac{x-4}{3}) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =12(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$
